title: Agreeing on the Answer but Not the Reason: Measurement Limits of LLM Reasoning Failure Taxonomies
abstract: arXiv:2611.13140v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Failure taxonomies for LLM reasoning are increasingly reported as measurements: papers state what fraction of a model's errors fall into named categories, then compare those fractions across models. We show that for one such category the reported fraction is largely a property of the measurement procedure. We defined Compositional Collapse (a model notices a required sub-part of a problem, then drops or misapplies it) and measured it across twelve models and eleven languages on a public multilingual math benchmark (2,316 graded records). First, 50.1% of failures carry evidence for more than one category, so the reported plurality depends on the order in which the classifier tests them: reversing two tests moves it in eleven of twelve models, and across all six orderings Collapse's share spans 26.4% to 76.4%. Second, agreement collapses for the category but not for the task. Native speakers of all eleven languages judged 179 transcripts,

translated_title: 答案一致但理由不一：大语言模型推理失败分类体系的测量局限性
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）推理失败分类体系正越来越多地被当作测量结果来报告：论文会声明模型错误中有多少比例落入某些命名类别，然后在模型之间比较这些比例。我们证明，对于其中一个类别，所报告的比例在很大程度上是测量方法本身的属性。我们定义了“组合崩塌”（Compositional Collapse，即模型注意到问题所需的某个子部分，随后又将其丢弃或错误应用），并在一个公开的多语言数学基准上跨越十二个模型和十一种语言进行了测量（共2,316条评分记录）。首先，50.1%的失败案例包含支持不止一个类别的证据，因此所报告的多数比例取决于分类器测试各类别的顺序：仅交换两个测试的顺序就会使该比例在十二个模型中的十一个里发生变化，而在所有六种排序下，“组合崩塌”的占比在26.4%到76.4%之间波动。其次，标注一致性在该类别层面崩溃，但在任务层面并未崩溃。来自全部十一种语言的母语者对179份记录进行了评判……
tldr: 该论文表明，LLM推理失败分类的测量结果很大程度上取决于测量程序本身：过半失败案例可归入多个类别，类别占比随分类器测试顺序大幅波动（26.4%–76.4%），且人工标注者对类别归属的共识远低于对任务答案正确性的共识。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that reported fractions in LLM reasoning failure taxonomies are largely artifacts of the measurement procedure itself—over half of failures support multiple categories, category shares swing dramatically (26.4%–76.4%) with classifier test ordering, and human annotator agreement collapses at the category level but not at the task level.
